chapter: Changes in the New York scene
title: The New York scene in 1987: bebop and the young lions
summary: When she arrived bebop was king; she played with the Twelve Tone Funk Orchestra, and teachers saw Wynton Marsalis as jazz police.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What changed in the New York scene from the time you arrived like and the next fifteen or twenty years?

Well the New York scene, I mean there are a lot of different scenes. So you know there’s the free scene, and if you’re just talking about jazz okay, but then there are all the other things like salsa and everything, but in jazz there’s the free scene and I played with this group called the Twelve Tone Funk Orchestra when I first got there, it was so much fun. But the straight ahead, you know the predominant jazz scene was basically a bebop scene. And that was when Wynton Marsalis and all the young lions came out and it was sort of like — when he came out it was sort of the people at the New School, the teachers and stuff referred to him sort of like the jazz police. This is the way, this is it, and they all wore suits and it was a very — he took what was sort of — I mean everybody did play bebop but he took what was like a more open thing and made it, I thought, and they thought, a much more rigid into the parameters. But bebop was king for sure when I moved to New York. And everybody played bebop and everybody that I — the people that I knew, the masters that I knew, and they had their own things but it was definitely bebop.
